title: The Sin No One Talks About in Sodom and Gomorrah
paragraphs: The Sin No One Talks About in Sodom and Gomorrah
They were not destroyed because they were poor.
They were destroyed because they were proud.
Because their stomachs were full, but their hearts were empty.
Because their city had comfort, luxury, noise, and pleasure…

“Behold, this was the guilt of your sister Sodom: she and her daughters had pride, excess of food, and prosperous ease, but did not aid the poor and needy.”
— Ezekiel 16:49
Before the fire fell, pride was already burning inside them.
And they used it all to forget God.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
Sodom was not just wicked in private.
Sodom became proud of what should have broken them.
And when God sent angels to rescue Lot, the city revealed what it had become.
Sodom was not judged because God was impatient.
Sodom was judged because God had seen enough.

“The outcry against Sodom and Gomorrah is great and their sin is very grave.”
— Genesis 18:20
Even when culture calls it freedom.
Even when people rename rebellion as identity.
And this is where it gets personal.
You can live in a modern Sodom without living in ancient Sodom.
You can have food, comfort, entertainment, money, lust, pride, and still have no repentance.
You can say, “I’m not that bad,” while your heart grows colder every day.
The sin no one talks about in Sodom was not only perversion.
And that road still ends in fire.
Jesus stepped into the judgment sinners deserved.
The fire that should have fallen on us fell on Christ at the cross.

“For our sake He made Him to be sin who knew no sin, so that in Him we might become the righteousness of God.”
— 2 Corinthians 5:21
You are not saved by pretending you are better than Sodom.
You are saved by repenting and running to Jesus.

“Repent therefore, and turn back, that your sins may be blotted out.”
— Acts 3:19
Lot was pulled out by mercy.
But do not confuse delay with permission.
Do not confuse comfort with approval.
Do not confuse God’s patience with weakness.

“The Lord is… patient toward you, not wishing that any should perish, but that all should reach repentance.”
— 2 Peter 3:9
